operations.description:
Restore a deleted todo from trash back to the member's active todo list.

This operation allows an authenticated member to recover one of their own private todo items after it has been moved to trash. In the underlying todo_app_todos model, a todo remains the same record throughout its lifecycle and the trash state is represented by the deleted_at column. Restoring the todo clears that deleted-state marker so the item is no longer treated as a trash entry and appears again in the member's normal todo list. The restored todo keeps its original task data, including the required title, optional description, optional start date, optional due date, completion flag, completion timestamp, creation timestamp, and update timestamp.

Access to this operation is restricted to the authenticated member who owns the todo through todo_app_member_id. A member must never be able to restore another member's todo. If the specified todo does not belong to the requesting member, the request must be rejected as unavailable or forbidden according to the service's error policy. This preserves the application's private ownership boundary in which each member manages only their own profile and todos.

The operation is specifically for todos that are currently in trash. Business rules require deleted todos to be excluded from the normal list and shown only in the trash context while deleted_at is set. If a member attempts to restore a todo that is not currently deleted, the request must be rejected because the restore action is only valid for a todo already in the deleted state. On success, the todo returns to the active list rather than creating a new replacement record.

This restore behavior also preserves the relationship between todo_app_todos and todo_app_todo_edit_histories. The todo's edit history remains associated with the same todo after recovery and continues to be available as part of that todo's lifecycle. Direct creation, modification, or deletion of history entries is not exposed by the API, so this endpoint changes only the todo's deleted-state marker and active-list availability.

This endpoint is typically used after the member has already browsed deleted items through the trash-list operation and selected a specific todo to recover. After this operation succeeds, normal todo-list and todo-detail operations should treat the restored item as active again, while trash-oriented operations should no longer include it.

If the todo exists but deleted_at is already null, reject the request as an invalid restore attempt because the todo is not in trash.

On success, update the row in a single write operation by setting deleted_at to null and updating updated_at to the current timestamp. Do not modify title, description, start_date, due_date, completed, completed_at, or created_at as part of restoration. Do not create a new todo record.

No manual history entry should be created solely for this restore action unless a separate cross-cutting audit mechanism exists outside this domain model.

Return the refreshed todo entity after the update. The response mapping should reflect the restored active state, including deleted_at as null. Ensure subsequent active-list queries include this todo again and trash-list queries exclude it after restoration.

Retrieve the edit history entries for a single todo that belongs to the authenticated member.

This operation provides the full TodoEditHistory view for one member-owned todo inside the private todo workspace. The history entity represents the chronological record of edits made to a todo, and each entry is presented with its recorded edit time. When a history entry captured changes to editable values such as title, description, start date, or due date, the response should expose only the values that were actually recorded for that edit event.

Access is limited to the authenticated member who owns the target todo. Before returning any history data, the service must verify that the referenced todo exists and is owned by the current member account. Todo history is private account data, so a signed-out caller must be rejected and a caller must never be allowed to view history for another member's todo.

The result is intended for history review after a member has created and later revised a todo. Entries must be presented from most recent to oldest so the caller can inspect the latest changes first. If the todo has never been edited after creation, the operation should return an empty paginated result and must not fabricate change records or imply that unchanged values were edited.

This operation is part of the broader todo maintenance flow. A client will commonly retrieve or inspect the parent todo first, then call this endpoint to review the sequence of past edits for that same todo. History remains available while the related todo exists, including when the todo is in trash, and becomes unavailable after the todo has been permanently removed.

7. Return the single mapped DTO.
